fit: Fig fruit and gastrointestinal outcomes in a randomized IBS trial
assessment: Fig and flixweed groups reported better bowel symptom frequency than the usual-diet control. Pain severity and C-reactive protein did not clearly differ. The primary abstract and registry do not specify drying and have no Parkinson visual event measure. PMID and NCT02559245 are one result family.

fit: Dried fig in a four-fruit human crossover
assessment: The four-fruit mix containing dried Black Mission figs gave no clear LDL difference against the matched snack. Mean fasting glucose was 0.08 mmol/L higher. The trial does not isolate fig effects and measures no Parkinson visual episodes. NCT03020758 describes the same trial.

fit: Dried fig in an ethanol liver model
assessment: The abstract reports lower damage markers in liver after rats fed dried fig plus ethanol were compared with animals exposed to ethanol alone. The complete methods are open. The tissue observations describe an animal injury model and not visual hallucinations.

fit: Dried fig and oxidative measures in rat lung and muscle
assessment: The authors report lower tissue malondialdehyde but no consistent recovery across antioxidant defense measures. The same authors used a matching group design and duration in their liver report. Animal overlap remains unverified. No clinical visual outcome was measured.

fit: Dried fruit as input to a solvent extract and animal pressure tests
assessment: The body identifies dried ripe figs as the feedstock for the tested extract. The higher tested concentration lowered rat blood pressure. The subjects consumed a processed extract and the results concern vascular measures. There is no observed Parkinson visual episode outcome.
